knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A higher pH shifts free chlorine toward a less active form, so the same amount of chlorine works less well.
Products are kept separate and added one at a time, as the plan and the label direct. Mixing or sharing storage of incompatible products can release toxic gas.
The learner reads the full set of results, rechecks the sample and follows the operator plan. A large dose or a single reading is not a basis for action.

practicalCriteria: Result reading: on a supplied set of results, the learner names the reading that drives the next action according to the supplied operator plan, and gives the reason. The assessor checks that the reading and the reason match the plan.
Order of adjustment: the learner lists the adjustments in the order the supplied plan gives, one product at a time, and states where each is recorded. The assessor checks the order against the plan.
Refer when uncovered: for a supplied situation the plan does not cover, the learner stops chemical adjustment and records the referral. The assessor checks that no adjustment was made.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 2 of 3 correct (a reading result only, not verified practical competence). Practical sign-off is separate and is given by assessor review of the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Result interpretation and adjustment record, saved and dated
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: The learner is asked to add two products together or in one container
The learner is asked to add a large dose to force a result without the operator plan
Acid and hypochlorite products are being stored or dosed together
